current_scene.text: Nine minutes to launch and the wind is doing something the forecast did not promise. You are the pad recovery tech, which today means you are the person who walks toward the thing everyone else walks away from. Your radio is already busy. [LOC:Launch Control] wants eyes on the tower.

loc-a.text: Inside [LOC:Launch Control] nobody is shouting, which is how you know it is going badly. The flight director is reading a number off a screen twice. On the wall, the booster sits lit from below like a monument that has not decided yet what it commemorates. [KEY:T-minus four minutes.]

loc-b.text: At [LOC:Tower Base] the sound arrives before the light does, through the concrete, up through your boots. The booster is coming back down. The arms of the tower open like someone preparing to catch a falling child, which is exactly what this is, at scale.

loc-c.text: The [POI:press pen] is a line of tripods and cold coffee. A reporter asks you, on record, whether it is safe. You have a company answer and a real answer and about two seconds to decide which one this person deserves.

loc-d.text: In the [LOC:Recovery Bay] the booster is horizontal and ticking as it cools. It is the least dramatic it will ever look and the most dangerous it has been all day. Someone has to sign the sheet that says the vehicle is safed. The pen is in your hand.

loc-e.text: The [LOC:berm] is the last place anyone stands before the pad becomes the pad. From up here the whole site is laid out like a diagram of itself. Someone has left a folding chair facing the tower, which is either sentiment or a very long shift.

loc-a.text: Call the wind violation out loud
Let the flight director get there first
Ask for the pad camera feed

loc-b.text: Hold position and watch the catch
Fall back behind the blast berm
Radio the arm alignment you can see

loc-c.text: Give the reporter the real answer
Say nothing and point at the press officer

loc-d.text: Walk the vehicle one more time first
Refuse until the vent cycle completes

loc-e.text: Sit in the chair a while
Log the debris you can see
Call it a day and go home

ending.title: Booster caught, third attempt
ending.summary: You stayed at the tower for the catch and told a reporter the truth before the press office had agreed on one. The vehicle came home. Your name is on the safing sheet, thirty seconds later than it should have been, because you walked it one more time.

canon.title: Launch on the second window
canon.summary: Winds held inside limits and the vehicle flew at the reopened window.

canon.title: Boostback burn nominal
canon.summary: The booster turned and burned back toward the pad on schedule.

canon.title: Tower catch succeeds
canon.summary: The arms took the booster cleanly on the third attempt in the programme.

canon.title: Vehicle safed after extended vent
canon.summary: Safing ran long; residual pressure delayed the sign-off.

canon.title: Site cleared for the next stack
canon.summary: The pad was walked, debris logged, and the site handed to the next crew.

player.what_you_did: You flagged the wind and deferred to the flight director.
You called the arm alignment from the tower base.
You held position and watched it come down.
You refused to sign until the vent cycle finished.
You logged the debris from the berm before leaving.
